hypotheses.mechanism: Causative variants in MYH7, TTN, and TNNT2 directly disrupt cardiac sarcomere structure and contractile function. MYH7 encodes the motor protein beta-myosin heavy chain, TNNT2 encodes the calcium-sensitive tropomyosin-binding subunit of troponin, and TTN encodes the giant sarcomere scaffolding protein titin. Mutations in these three genes account for a substantial fraction of genetic DCM through loss of contractile integrity. TTN truncations are established as a primary DCM mechanism (PMID:22335739), and TNNT2 mutations affect DCM progression in children (PMID:42496620).
hypotheses.title: Sarcomere structural defect drives DCM through MYH7, TTN, and TNNT2 dysfunction

hypotheses.mechanism: LMNA mutations disrupt nuclear envelope integrity, impairing mechanotransduction in cardiomyocytes. Lamin A/C is essential for nuclear envelope structure in cardiac cells (P02545). LMNA variants cause DCM with high penetrance (PMID:PPR1285401). TTN truncations independently cause DCM by destabilizing sarcomere architecture (PMID:22335739). The co-occurrence of LMNA and TTN variants in DCM patients reflects two independent mechanistic pathways—nuclear envelope integrity and sarcomere structure—both converging on cardiomyocyte mechanical failure.
hypotheses.title: Nuclear envelope and sarcomere defects converge via LMNA and TTN to cause DCM

hypotheses.mechanism: RBM20 is an RNA-binding protein that regulates splicing of TTN and other cardiac structural genes (Q5T481). RBM20 mutations cause DCM characterized by malignant ventricular arrhythmia and subendocardial fibrosis (PMID:41817671). By disrupting the precisely controlled isoform switching of titin required for cardiac development and stress response, RBM20 deficiency alters TTN mRNA processing. The RBM20-TTN axis represents a regulatory layer superimposed on structural proteins, where splicing defects in TTN and other targets drive DCM pathology.
hypotheses.title: RBM20-TTN splicing axis regulates DCM through isoform switching
